pulls.title: 6988055: Support IDNA2008
pulls.author: arnt
pulls.body_excerpt: `java.net.IDN` still implements IDNA2003, which is frozen at Unicode 3.2. This PR moves it to UTS46 (IDNA2008 with the Unicode compatibility mapping), which is what the big three browsers and most other languages' IDN libraries use. Names such as faß.de have been registrable since 2010, and today `IDN` turns that into fass.de, which is a different domain. ### Changes The implementation is ICU4J's UTS46 code, merged into `jdk.internal.icu` with the smallest reasonable diff. The UTS46 data (`uts46.nrm`) is generated from Unicode 17, the same version as `Character`, so `IDN` can follow future Uni

pulls.title: 8389741: [VectorAPI] Intrinsify Float16Vector.rearrange operations
pulls.author: jatin-bhateja
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi All, Currently Float16Vector.rearrange operations are not intrinsified and are executed through the fallback implementation. rearrange is a pure lane-permutation (data movement) operation; it never interprets the 16-bit lane bits as an IEEE binary16 number. Since a Float16 lane maps to T_SHORT, it reuses the existing 16-bit vector permute backend directly. Patch adds Add intrinsification support encompassing the following tasks: - Inline expander extension: allow LT_FLOAT16 past the lane-type guard in inline_vector_rearrange all downstream logic already resolves to the T_SHORT permute path.

pulls.title: 8392927: RISC-V: explicitly narrow unsigned subword types in extract_v
pulls.author: mhaessig
pulls.body_excerpt: This PR explicitly narrows the result of `extract_v` if the result is an unsigned subword type, i.e. `char` or `boolean`. pulls.author: devnexen
pulls.body_excerpt: Follow-up to JDK-8388592, suggested by @merykitty in the review there. get_early_ctrl() hoists expensive nodes by calling get_early_ctrl_for_expensive(), which rewires their control input. pulls.author: raneashay
pulls.body_excerpt: Prior to this patch, the `StackYellowPages` and `StackRedPages` influenced the total reserved stack memory, but they didn't change the minimum stack size specified as required by HotSpot to Windows. This patch adds the call to `SetThreadStackGuarantee()` to set the minimum stack size. The key change here is that the argument to `SetThreadStackGuarantee()` is set to one less than the total number of yellow pages. pulls.title: 8317510: Change Windows debug symbol files naming to avoid losing info when an executable and a library share the same name
pulls.author: fthevenet
pulls.body_excerpt: When building OpenJDK on Windows using "--with-native-debug-info=external", the resulting debug symbols are saved in files located in the same folder as the corresponding executable or library and named by swapping the extension ".exe" or ".dll" for a ".pdb" one (or "diz" if option "--with-native-debug-info=zipped" is used), which means that in the event of an exe and a dll file sharing the same target folder and file name (e.g. `bin\java.exe` and `bin\java.dll`), we have to choose whether symbols in `bin\java.pdb` will refer to the exe or the dll; we can't have both.
